blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and September 2026, detached houses: listings fell from 29 in June to 25 in September (−13.8%), and it took 6.0% of the city’s 215 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings rose from 5 in June to 7 in September (+40.0%), and it took 1.3% of the city’s 318 sales over the period.
The monthly write-ups singled out Aberdeen for detached houses in August (a sellers’ best bet); detached houses in July (a buyers’ best bet).

items.t: Fee-simple lots are the default — effectively the only — form: The housing stock is overwhelmingly single-detached houses on rural and agricultural lots; homes are effectively all freehold farm and rural residential lots. Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014 applies, including the Section 200 agricultural zones: in the Agricultural One Zone (A1) the minimum subdivision lot area is 8.0 ha and in the Agricultural Two Zone (A2) it is 16.0 ha — the lot's zone for a single parcel is shown in the City's WebMap. Zoning at that scale does not produce subdivision lots or condo buildings.

Bare-land strata: none verified — count 0: The only strata housing confirmed anywhere in the sub-area is one built townhome complex (below) — built strata, not bare-land strata, and never lot stock. Where a bare-land strata lot did exist, the buyer would own the lot as a strata lot: strata fees and bylaws apply to the lot itself, and the purchase runs on a Form B (SPA s.

Assemblies / proposals — documented as plans, never as inventory: The governing documents are the plan framework itself: Abbotsforward 2050 (no Aberdeen neighbourhood plan) and the City's AgRefresh agriculture work (A1 Uplands / A2 Lowlands patterns, 8 ha / 16 ha minimums). A designation is not an approval and no site is listed as inventory here.

ALR vs non-ALR split: the research states rural Aberdeen parcels are in or beside the Agricultural Land Reserve, in words only — no percentage is published, so no split figure is stated. Subdivision, non-farm use and added dwellings on an ALR parcel need both City zoning compliance and, where the ALR Use Regulation requires it, Agricultural Land Commission approval; per-parcel ALR status is UNCONFIRMED until checked.

Added dwellings on farm lots (the Aberdeen substitute for "more units"): the City-hosted A1 zone section permits one Accessory Farm Dwelling Unit per lot in accordance with the ALR Use Regulation, B.C. Reg. These are farm dwellings, not strata lots, and cannot be sold separately.

Servicing: rural residential lots outside the urban boundary may use wells and onsite sewage rather than community water and sewer — per-parcel servicing is confirmed from the parcel's well record (provincial GWELLS) and its onsite-sewage filing, not assumed from the address.

Airport overlay on the land itself: Aberdeen sits north/northeast of YXX; land covered by the Abbotsford Airport Zoning Regulations (AZR), SOR/83-253, shown on City drawing M-500, is subject to height limits, and a developer on AZR land must obtain NAV CANADA and Transport Canada approvals before the City issues a building permit. Property-level AZR status for any single lot: UNVERIFIED.
Floodplain: Zoning Bylaw Schedule E sets floodplain boundaries; the floodplain status of any single Aberdeen lot must be checked for that lot: UNVERIFIED per parcel.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Aberdeen

items.t: "Aberdeen" is both the board sub-area name in the SnapStats FVR September 2026 report and an official City name — profile area 6 in the City's 2020 Demographic Profiles, separate from Bradner – Mt. Lehman (area 1) and West Abbotsford (area 7). Exact boundary roads for the sub-area are not published in text form on a City source: UNVERIFIED.

Nearby areas: Bradner and Mt. Lehman to the west and northwest, Abbotsford West / Clearbrook to the east, Poplar to the northeast, and Aldergrove (Township of Langley) further west along Fraser Highway.

Main roads and commute: Bradner Road (north–south through the area), Fraser Highway (north edge), Mt. Lehman Road to the west, and Huntingdon Road and King Road to the south toward YXX and the Huntingdon / Sumas border crossing; Highway 1 is reached via the Mt. Lehman Road and Clearbrook Road interchanges to the north — the route west toward Langley, Surrey and Vancouver and east toward Chilliwack. Published official drive-time figures: UNVERIFIED.

Transit: BC Transit route 21 (Aldergrove / Abbotsford) runs along Fraser Highway at the north edge toward Bourquin Exchange; no local route was verified running through the interior rural roads, and the nearest exchanges are Bourquin Exchange, Clearbrook Centre and Highstreet Transit Exchange.

Schools: Aberdeen Elementary, 2975 Bradner Road, is the public elementary school physically inside the sub-area (Ministry-listed name/address). Catchment, single-address only: the recorded SD34 locator run for 2975 Bradner Road (the school's own address) returns Aberdeen Elementary → Eugene Reimer Middle → Rick Hansen Secondary; Eugene Reimer Middle's family-of-schools page lists Aberdeen Elementary among its feeder schools and names Rick Hansen Secondary (Grades 9–12) as that family's secondary school. Ministry-listed addresses for the chain: Eugene Reimer Middle School, 3433 Firhill Dr (in Abbotsford West, recorded only as the middle school's address, not as an Aberdeen sample); Rick Hansen Secondary, 31150 Blueridge Dr. Catchments for any other Aberdeen address are UNVERIFIED — run the exact address. Catchment areas are set under SD34 Policy 18.

Recreation, libraries, shopping and health: no City park inside Aberdeen was verified by name and address on the City parks list; the nearest verified City facilities are Matsqui Recreation Centre, 3106 Clearbrook Road, and Clearbrook Park, 3680 Clearbrook Road, to the east. Libraries: Mt. Lehman Library, 5875 Mt. Lehman Road (northwest), and Clearbrook Library, 32320 George Ferguson Way (east), both Fraser Valley Regional Library. No shopping centre or grocery store inside Aberdeen was verified on an official source; the nearest verified centres are Highstreet Shopping Centre at Mt. Lehman Road and the Clearbrook / South Fraser Way commercial area. Nearest hospital: Abbotsford Regional Hospital and Cancer Centre, 32900 Marshall Road; nearest urgent and primary care centre: 100-2692 Clearbrook Road.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Aberdeen

items.t: Zoning: Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014 governs: Confirm the parcel's zone in the City's WebMap before assuming any use is permitted.
OCP: Abbotsforward 2050, the CURRENT Official Community Plan, governs; there is no Aberdeen neighbourhood plan

SSMUH / suites / coach houses (Abbotsford specifics): the zoning bylaw's s. 140 small-scale multi-unit provision allows 3 units on lots 280 m² or less and 4 units on lots greater than 280 m² in the stated conditions, and s. 140.3.8 states one secondary suite is permitted in all single detached dwellings; the suite size cap is under 50% of the size of the principal unit, and a coach/garden suite is capped at 15% of the lot area to a maximum of 100 m² (Abbotsford only figures).

ALR block — full form (Aberdeen's governing land regime): subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval, and ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Information Bulletin 09, s. 6; Strata Property Act, s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act, s. 21(1)). Farm class (BC Assessment) in full three-tier form: $2,500 of gross farm income at 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 ha above that; $10,000 under 0.8 ha — applications by October 31.

Airport Zoning Regulations: where a lot is inside the AZR area on City drawing M-500, building height may not exceed the approach, outer or transitional surfaces, and NAV CANADA and Transport Canada approvals are required before a City building permit — check before planning a tall shop or barn. Per-lot status: UNVERIFIED.

BC strata block — applies in full to the one strata complex here (Lantern Park resales) and to any strata lot a buyer is redirected to: Form B (SPA s. 123.1/123.2 + Reg 7.01, May 1, 2023 exemptions); a "45+" listing line is NOT a valid age bylaw. Lantern Park is recorded as NOT age-restricted, and no 55+ strata was verified in Aberdeen.

First-home programs — the land boundary, with the date discrepancy stated in-line: the First-Time Home Buyers' GST rebate (Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026 per CRA — this date governs) rebates 100% of the GST on new HOUSING up to $1 million (maximum $50,000), phasing out to $1.5 million, agreements March 20, 2025–2031 — new housing, NOT bare land. The GST New Housing Rebate is 36%, maximum $6,300, $350,000–$450,000 phase-out. Home Buyers' Plan $60,000 per buyer; First Home Savings Account $8,000 per year to $40,000 lifetime.

Abbotsford has a Supreme Court registry. Court-ordered sales and foreclosure matters for Aberdeen land can run through the Supreme Court registry in Abbotsford itself — relevant context for any court-sale acreage purchase.

The airport's height rules are drawn on a City map, not in the listing. The AZR area is shown on City drawing M-500; a tall shop or barn planned without checking that drawing can fail at the permit stage, after NAV CANADA and Transport Canada approvals are already owed.
The middle school in this area's only documented catchment chain is not in this area.

The second Abbotsford tax penalty lands September 16, not early September. Taxes due July 2, 2026; 5% on July 3, 2026 and a further 5% on September 16, 2026 — a farm closing straddling those dates carries any unpaid penalty in the adjustments.

faq.q: Is there bus service through Aberdeen?
faq.a: BC Transit route 21 (Aldergrove / Abbotsford) runs on Fraser Highway at the north edge toward Bourquin Exchange; no route through the interior rural roads was verified on the BC Transit system map.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Aberdeen than in June?
faq.a: In Aberdeen, listings of houses fell from 29 in June to 25 in September (−13.8%); condos and townhomes rose from 5 in June to 7 in September (+40.0%).

faq.q: How big is Aberdeen compared with the rest of Abbotsford?
faq.a: In September 2026, Aberdeen held 5.7% of the 440 houses listed in Abbotsford and 1.2% of the 572 condos and townhomes listed in Abbotsford.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Aberdeen from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 13 houses and 4 condos and townhomes sold in Aberdeen over those 4 months.

faq.q: Can I buy a bare building lot in Aberdeen?
faq.a: There is no subdivision-lot product to buy — no named bare-land subdivision offering, bare-land strata plan or presale lot offering exists here. What trades is fee-simple farm and rural residential parcels, at agricultural scale (A1 subdivision minimum 8.0 ha; A2, 16.0 ha).

faq.q: Where exactly is Aberdeen — is it part of Langley or Mission?
faq.a: Neither. It is a City of Abbotsford community and board sub-area: the rural ground around Bradner Road, south of Fraser Highway and west of Clearbrook, north of YXX — profile area 6 in the City's own demographic profiles, separate from Bradner – Mt. Lehman and West Abbotsford. Aldergrove (Langley) is further west along Fraser Highway.

faq.q: Can I subdivide a farm parcel here?
faq.a: Price subdivision expectations from the zone, not the frontage: A1 lots subdivide at a minimum of 8.0 ha and A2 at 16.0 ha, and on ALR land subdivision also needs Agricultural Land Commission approval. Confirm the parcel's zone in the City WebMap and its ALR status before valuing any split.

faq.q: Can a second home be added for family or farm workers?
faq.a: In the A1 zone, one Accessory Farm Dwelling Unit per lot under the ALR Use Regulation (or as approved by the ALC), on a lot of at least 0.4 ha, to 90 m² on lots of 40 ha or less and 186 m² on lots over 40 ha; one secondary suite per lot (to 100 m² in the A1 section; Abbotsford's general suite cap is under 50% of the principal unit, coach/garden 15% of lot to max 100 m²). It is a farm dwelling — it cannot be stratified or sold separately.

faq.q: Does the airport restrict building on my lot?
faq.a: Where the lot is inside the Airport Zoning Regulation area on City drawing M-500, yes: height may not exceed the approach, outer or transitional surfaces, and NAV CANADA and Transport Canada approvals are needed before a City building permit. Per-lot status must be checked — it does not follow from the street address alone.
